- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; adjust downward by 2–5% relative to recent low.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and history shows mean reversion, model often fails to revert; add a “mean-reversion bias” term: forecast = prior 10-day avg + 0.3×(true - prior avg) if deviation > 3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early volatility (first 5 days deviate >5% from forecast), reduce forecast slope for next 3 days to avoid overcommitting to trend.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.7→0.9) but price is flat or falling, model often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
